```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7)
```

```{r libs, message = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(PKNCA)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

This vignette validates the `Chu_2016_vegf165b_human_qsp` model against its
source.

* Reference: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Chu_2016_vegf165b_human_qsp"))$reference`

The paper extends the Popel-lab three-compartment model of vascular
endothelial growth factor (VEGF) to peripheral arterial disease (PAD). The
three compartments are normal tissue (all tissues and organs except blood and
the diseased calf), blood, and the ischemic calf muscle. For the first time in
this model family, the anti-angiogenic splice variant VEGF165b is tracked next
to the pro-angiogenic VEGF165a and VEGF121. VEGF165b binds VEGFR1, VEGFR2,
soluble VEGFR1 (sVEGFR1), alpha-2-macroglobulin and the heparan-sulfate (GAG)
sites of the extracellular matrix. It does not bind neuropilin-1 (NRP1).

The paper prints the parameter tables (Tables 2-5) and gives the equations as
images in Supplementary File 1. It also ships the authors' **SimBiology model
as an SBML export (Supplementary File 2)**. That export is the model the authors
ran, so the packaged model is a mechanical translation of it:

* 152 ODE states, one per SBML species that takes part in a reaction;
* 410 reactions, each kept as one named flux `J_<SBML reaction name>` with the
  rate law exactly as exported;
* 249 derived constants (SBML initial assignments and assignment rules) and 153
  base parameters, all `fixed()` in `ini()`.

The SBML rate constants are per second. The packaged model runs in **hours**:
every mass balance is multiplied by `sec_per_hr = 3600`, and the rate constants
keep the per-second values printed in the paper. Species amounts are in mol per
cm3 of compartment. The `*_pM` outputs are the authors' own SBML rules for free
concentrations in interstitial fluid (tissues) or plasma (blood).

This is an **endogenous steady-state model**: there is no dosing, and no
between-subject or residual variability. Receptors and GAG sites start at their
SBML initial amounts and the VEGF species start at zero. Validation therefore
uses steady-state checks, not NCA. PKNCA is loaded only to follow the package's vignette template.

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Chu_2016_vegf165b_human_qsp"))
length(mod$state)
stopifnot(length(mod$state) == 152)
# An explicit-ODE model must not be auto-converted to a linear compartment solve.
stopifnot(is.null(mod$linCmt))
```

## Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
p <- mod$population
data.frame(
  Field = c("Species", "Disease state", "Notes"),
  Value = c(p$species, p$disease_state, p$notes)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Population metadata (Chu 2016 Methods and Table 2).")
```

The model is not fitted to individual patients. Geometry for the normal-tissue
and blood compartments comes from the authors' earlier human model (Finley and
Popel 2012). The diseased compartment is the combined lateral and medial
gastrocnemius and soleus muscles of a PAD patient: 738 cm3, with the fluid
fractions and muscle-fibre surface area of Table 2. The authors chose the
fractions of VEGF165 secreted as VEGF165b (0.1 in normal tissue, 0.1 for
endothelial cells, 1.0 in PAD calf). With these values VEGF stays inside the
0-10 pM interstitial range measured in PAD muscle (Hoier 2013), and VEGF165b
dominates in PAD calf as it does in patient biopsies.

## Source trace

Every base parameter in `ini()` carries a trailing comment naming its source.
"Suppl. 2 SBML" means the value is taken from the SimBiology export. Where the
paper also prints the value, the table or text location is given as well. The
table below is built from those comments.

```{r source-trace}
src <- readLines(system.file(
  "modeldb", "endogenous", "Chu_2016_vegf165b_human_qsp.R",
  package = "nlmixr2lib"
))
ini_lines <- grep("<- fixed\\(", src, value = TRUE)
trace <- data.frame(
  Parameter = trimws(sub("<-.*", "", ini_lines)),
  Value = sub(".*fixed\\(([^)]*)\\).*", "\\1", ini_lines),
  Source = trimws(sub(".*\\) # ", "", ini_lines))
)
stopifnot(nrow(trace) == 153, all(nzchar(trace$Source)))
knitr::kable(trace, caption = "Base parameters and their sources.")
```

| Model element | Source |
|---|---|
| Compartment layout (normal, blood, PAD calf), transport by permeability, lymph and clearance | Methods 'Three-compartment models'; Figure 7; Suppl. 2 SBML |
| VEGF isoform / receptor binding network (VEGF165b binds R1, R2, sR1, GAG; not NRP1) | Methods 'Binding of VEGF165a, VEGF165b and VEGF121'; Figure 8; Suppl. 2 SBML |
| All 410 rate laws, 249 derived constants and initial amounts | Suppl. 2 SBML (reactions, initial assignments, assignment rules) |
| Free-concentration outputs (`*_pM`) and receptors per cell (`*_num`) | Suppl. 2 SBML assignment rules |
| Secretion ratios VEGF165b / total VEGF165 = 0.1, 0.1, 1.0 | Conclusions; Suppl. 2 SBML |

## Steady state

```{r steady-state}
ev <- rxode2::et(c(0, 10, 24, 48, 100, 500, 1000, 10000, 20000))
sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, atol = 1e-30, rtol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6))

out_cols <- c(
  "dis_V165_pM", "dis_V165b_pM", "dis_V121_pM",
  "bld_V165_pM", "bld_V165b_pM", "bld_V121_pM",
  "nrm_V165_pM", "nrm_V165b_pM", "nrm_V121_pM"
)
ss <- sim[sim$time == 20000, ]
ss_10k <- sim[sim$time == 10000, ]
rel_change <- abs(unlist(ss[out_cols]) / unlist(ss_10k[out_cols]) - 1)
max(rel_change)
# Steady-state hold: the outputs no longer move between 10,000 and 20,000 h.
stopifnot(max(rel_change) < 1e-6)
```

```{r approach-to-ss, fig.height = 4}
sim[sim$time > 0, ] |>
  dplyr::select(time, dplyr::all_of(out_cols)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "pM") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    compartment = factor(substr(output, 1, 3), c("nrm", "bld", "dis"), c("Normal", "Blood", "PAD calf")),
    isoform = sub("^[a-z]+_(V[0-9b]+)_pM$", "\\1", output)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, pM, colour = isoform)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~compartment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Free VEGF (pM)", colour = "Isoform",
       title = "Approach to the endogenous steady state from zero VEGF")
```

## Table 1: steady-state VEGF concentrations

Table 1 of the paper gives steady-state free concentrations for the final
secretion ratios. Every simulated value is inside the 0-10 pM constraint the
authors imposed.

```{r table1}
tab1 <- data.frame(
  Compartment = rep(c("PAD calf", "Blood", "Normal"), each = 3),
  Species = rep(c("VEGF165a", "VEGF165b", "VEGF121"), 3),
  column = out_cols,
  Published = c(1.276, 2.163, 0.701, 0.886, 1.863, 0.653, 4.591, 6.486, 2.416)
)
tab1$Simulated <- signif(unlist(ss[tab1$column]), 4)
tab1$pct_diff <- round(100 * (tab1$Simulated / tab1$Published - 1), 1)
tab1 |>
  dplyr::select(-column) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Published (pM)" = Published,
    "Simulated (pM)" = Simulated,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 1 of Chu 2016 (steady-state free VEGF).")

stopifnot(
  all(tab1$Simulated > 0 & tab1$Simulated < 10),
  # Normal tissue and PAD-calf VEGF165a reproduce Table 1.
  all(abs(tab1$pct_diff[tab1$Compartment == "Normal"]) < 3),
  abs(tab1$pct_diff[tab1$column == "dis_V165_pM"]) < 3
)
```

The deterministic solve matches the normal-tissue row to within 1.5%, and PAD
calf VEGF165a to within 0.5%. The blood row and the PAD-calf VEGF165b and
VEGF121 values come out **lower** than printed: blood VEGF165b by 26%, blood
VEGF121 by 22%, PAD-calf VEGF165b by 9%. The maintainers checked the obvious
explanations:

* switching each of the 410 reactions off in turn does not close the gap: the
  knockouts that agree best with Table 1 all leave blood VEGF165b at about
  1.37 pM;
* using the Table 3 receptor densities, or the Results-text endothelial
  secretion split (0.0279 / 0.0031), makes the fit worse;
* removing the redundant `*_Abluminal_*` reactions (see Assumptions) makes the
  fit worse;
* evaluating the nine initial assignments that read rule-set parameters
  (`S_NB_dis`, `VesselSA_Vol_blood_tis_dis`) with those parameters' stored
  placeholder value of 1 also makes the fit worse (blood VEGF165b 1.32 pM).

Figure 3 (below) shows the same gap: its blood VEGF165b curve sits above the
one simulated from the export. The export therefore seems to differ slightly
from the version used for Table 1 and Figure 3 in some blood-side setting.
The export's VEGF165b / VEGF165a ratios are 1.54 (PAD calf), 1.63 (blood) and
1.40 (normal). The Discussion prints 1.70, 2.10 and 1.41. The model is shipped
as exported; no parameter was tuned.

## Figure 3: secretion-ratio scans

Each row of Figure 3 varies the VEGF165b / total VEGF165 secretion ratio in one
compartment from 0 to 1, with the ratio held at 0.1 in the other two
compartments. Total VEGF165 secretion stays fixed.

```{r fig3-sim}
grid <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)
scan <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(varied = "normal", V165bSecretionRatio_Normal = grid,
             V165bSecretionRatio_Blood = 0.1, V165bSecretionRatio_Disease = 0.1),
  data.frame(varied = "blood", V165bSecretionRatio_Normal = 0.1,
             V165bSecretionRatio_Blood = grid, V165bSecretionRatio_Disease = 0.1),
  data.frame(varied = "disease", V165bSecretionRatio_Normal = 0.1,
             V165bSecretionRatio_Blood = 0.1, V165bSecretionRatio_Disease = grid)
)
scan$id <- seq_len(nrow(scan))
ratio <- scan$V165bSecretionRatio_Normal
ratio[scan$varied == "blood"] <- scan$V165bSecretionRatio_Blood[scan$varied == "blood"]
ratio[scan$varied == "disease"] <- scan$V165bSecretionRatio_Disease[scan$varied == "disease"]
scan$ratio <- ratio

scan_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, rxode2::et(20000),
  params = scan[, c("id", "V165bSecretionRatio_Normal", "V165bSecretionRatio_Blood",
                    "V165bSecretionRatio_Disease")],
  atol = 1e-30, rtol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6
))
# One parameter set per row with a shared event table: rxode2 labels the rows sim.id.
if (!"id" %in% names(scan_sim)) scan_sim$id <- scan_sim$sim.id
fig3 <- scan_sim |>
  dplyr::select(id, dplyr::all_of(out_cols)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(scan[, c("id", "varied", "ratio")], by = "id") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(out_cols), names_to = "output", values_to = "pM") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    compartment = factor(substr(output, 1, 3), c("nrm", "bld", "dis"), c("Normal", "Blood", "Disease")),
    isoform = sub("^[a-z]+_(V[0-9b]+)_pM$", "\\1", output),
    varied = factor(varied, c("normal", "blood", "disease"),
                    c("A: vary normal", "B: vary blood", "C: vary disease"))
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(isoform != "V121")
```

```{r fig3-plot, fig.height = 7}
ggplot(fig3, aes(ratio, pM, colour = isoform)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(varied ~ compartment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Secretion ratio of VEGF165b to total VEGF165",
       y = "Free concentration (pM)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Replicates Figure 3 of Chu 2016")
```

```{r fig3-check}
pick <- function(v, comp, iso, r) {
  fig3$pM[fig3$varied == v & fig3$compartment == comp & fig3$isoform == iso &
            abs(fig3$ratio - r) < 1e-9]
}
# Row C, left column: normal-tissue VEGF is insensitive to the PAD-calf ratio
# (Figure 3C reads about 4.6 pM VEGF165a and 6.4 pM VEGF165b over the whole range).
nrm_c_a <- fig3$pM[fig3$varied == "C: vary disease" & fig3$compartment == "Normal" & fig3$isoform == "V165"]
nrm_c_b <- fig3$pM[fig3$varied == "C: vary disease" & fig3$compartment == "Normal" & fig3$isoform == "V165b"]
range(nrm_c_a)
range(nrm_c_b)
stopifnot(
  diff(range(nrm_c_a)) / mean(nrm_c_a) < 0.01,
  diff(range(nrm_c_b)) / mean(nrm_c_b) < 0.02,
  # Row C, right column: PAD-calf VEGF165b overtakes VEGF165a near a ratio of
  # 0.3 and rises monotonically with the disease secretion ratio.
  all(diff(fig3$pM[fig3$varied == "C: vary disease" & fig3$compartment == "Disease" & fig3$isoform == "V165b"]) > 0),
  pick("C: vary disease", "Disease", "V165b", 0.2) < pick("C: vary disease", "Disease", "V165", 0.2),
  pick("C: vary disease", "Disease", "V165b", 0.4) > pick("C: vary disease", "Disease", "V165", 0.4),
  # Row A, left column: normal VEGF165b reaches about 41 pM at a normal ratio of 1.
  abs(pick("A: vary normal", "Normal", "V165b", 1) / 41 - 1) < 0.1,
  # Row B, left column: about 26 pM at a blood ratio of 1.
  abs(pick("B: vary blood", "Normal", "V165b", 1) / 26 - 1) < 0.1,
  # Row C, middle column: simulated blood VEGF165b stays near 1.37 pM (the
  # published curve rises from about 1.6 to 1.85 pM; see the Table 1 section).
  all(abs(fig3$pM[fig3$varied == "C: vary disease" & fig3$compartment == "Blood" & fig3$isoform == "V165b"] / 1.37 - 1) < 0.03)
)
```

The normal-tissue column reproduces Figure 3 in all three rows: about 41 pM
VEGF165b at a normal ratio of 1 (row A), about 26 pM at a blood ratio of 1
(row B), and no response to the PAD-calf ratio (row C). The PAD-calf column
reproduces the shapes, including the crossing of VEGF165a and VEGF165b at a
ratio of about 0.3 (row C), but its VEGF165b curves end 10-20% lower than
printed. The blood column also runs lower. In row C the published blood
VEGF165b rises from about 1.6 to 1.85 pM with the PAD-calf ratio, while the
simulated curve stays near 1.37 pM. This is the same difference as in Table 1.

## Figure 5: tissue VEGF distribution and receptor occupancy

The Results give the main percentages behind Figure 5 in the text. Percentages
of a ligand are over its free and bound forms in that compartment. For VEGFR1,
the receptor-coupled `R1:N1` complex is counted under NRP1, as in the Figure 5B
axis.

```{r fig5}
frac <- function(pre, target, pool) {
  v <- unlist(ss[paste0(pre, "_", pool)])
  100 * ss[[paste0(pre, "_", target)]] / sum(v)
}
v165 <- c("V165", "V165_MECM", "V165_MEBM", "V165_MPBM", "V165_R1", "V165_R2",
          "V165_N1", "V165_R2_N1", "V165_sR1")
v165b <- c("V165b", "V165b_MECM", "V165b_MEBM", "V165b_MPBM", "V165b_R1",
           "V165b_R2", "V165b_sR1")
v121_n <- c("V121", "V121_R1", "V121_R2", "V121_R1_N1", "V121_sR1", "V121_sR1_N1")
v121_d <- c(v121_n, "R2_V121")
r1 <- c("R1", "V165_R1", "V165b_R1", "V121_R1", "V121_R1_N1")
r2_n <- c("R2", "V165_R2", "V165b_R2", "V121_R2", "V165_R2_N1")
r2_d <- c(r2_n, "R2_V121")
n1 <- c("N1", "V165_N1", "V121_R1_N1", "R1_N1", "sR1_N1", "V121_sR1_N1", "V165_R2_N1")
sr1 <- c("sR1", "sR1_MECM", "sR1_MEBM", "sR1_MPBM", "V165_sR1", "V165b_sR1",
         "V121_sR1", "sR1_N1", "V121_sR1_N1")

fig5 <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "PAD calf VEGF165a bound to ECM", "PAD calf VEGF165a bound to PBM",
    "PAD calf VEGF165b bound to ECM", "PAD calf VEGF165b bound to PBM",
    "PAD calf VEGF121 as VEGF121:R1:N1", "Normal VEGF121 as VEGF121:R1:N1",
    "Normal VEGFR1 as VEGF121:R1:N1", "Normal VEGFR2 as VEGF165a:R2:N1",
    "PAD calf VEGFR2 as VEGF165a:R2:N1", "PAD calf NRP1 as R1:N1",
    "PAD calf sVEGFR1 bound to ECM", "PAD calf sVEGFR1 bound to EBM",
    "PAD calf sVEGFR1 bound to PBM"
  ),
  Published = c(55, 17, 62, 20, 48, 51, 33, 49, 20, 18, 62, 15, 19),
  Simulated = c(
    frac("dis", "V165_MECM", v165), frac("dis", "V165_MPBM", v165),
    frac("dis", "V165b_MECM", v165b), frac("dis", "V165b_MPBM", v165b),
    frac("dis", "V121_R1_N1", v121_d), frac("nrm", "V121_R1_N1", v121_n),
    frac("nrm", "V121_R1_N1", r1), frac("nrm", "V165_R2_N1", r2_n),
    frac("dis", "V165_R2_N1", r2_d), frac("dis", "R1_N1", n1),
    frac("dis", "sR1_MECM", sr1), frac("dis", "sR1_MEBM", sr1),
    frac("dis", "sR1_MPBM", sr1)
  )
)
fig5$Simulated <- round(fig5$Simulated, 1)
fig5 |>
  dplyr::rename("Published (%)" = Published, "Simulated (%)" = Simulated) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates the Figure 5 percentages quoted in the Chu 2016 Results.")
# Deterministic: no random draws, so the comparison is tight.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig5$Simulated - fig5$Published) < 2))
```

All 13 percentages quoted in the text are reproduced to within 2 percentage
points. These are steady-state ratios within each tissue compartment, so they
do not depend on the blood-side difference seen in Table 1.

## Assumptions and deviations

* **The SBML export is the model.** Where the export and the printed tables
  differ, the export is used, because it is what the authors simulated. The
  differences are:
  - Table 3 receptor densities (normal EC: 3,750 VEGFR1, 300 VEGFR2, 20,000
    NRP1; disease: 0, 0 and 34,500) are not the export's values. The export
    uses 550 / 350 / 17,500 per normal-tissue endothelial cell and 3,750 / 300 /
    20,000 in PAD calf, on both the abluminal and luminal sides. The Table 3
    values reproduce Table 1 much worse (normal VEGF121 0.46 instead of
    2.4 pM).
  - VEGF-GAG binding uses `koff = 6.9e-4 1/s` with `Kd = 23.8 nM`
    (`kon = 2.9e4 1/M/s`). Table 4 prints `kon = 4e5`, `koff = 1e-2` and a Kd of
    "23.8 pM". With `kon = 4e5` and `koff = 1e-2` the Kd is 25 nM, so the printed
    pM is a unit slip for nM.
  - The PAD-calf sVEGFR1 permeability is `1.5e-7 cm/s` (Table 5 prints
    `3.0e-7`). VEGF:sVEGFR1 complexes clear from plasma at the sVEGFR1 rate
    `5e-6 1/s` (Table 5 prints `3.0e-4`). VEGF165b:alpha-2-macroglobulin-fast
    complexes clear at the slow `c_a2M` rate.
  - Endothelial cells secrete 0.031 molecules/cell/s of VEGF165 plus
    0.00344 of VEGF121. The Results text describes 0.031 as the endothelial
    total including 10% VEGF121, which would give 0.0279 + 0.0031; that split
    matches Table 1 worse.
  - alpha-2-macroglobulin synthesis is `6.2776e-14 mol/cm3/s`
    (3.78e10 molecules/cm3/s). Table 5 prints 3.5e10.
  - Receptor internalization and insertion rates (`k_int`, `k_int_L`, `sR`,
    `sR_L` = 2.8e-4 1/s), lymph flow and the normal-tissue and blood geometry
    are not printed in the paper. They are taken from the export.
* **Redundant receptor reactions are kept.** Besides the mass-action binding,
  coupling and internalization reactions, the export has a set of
  `Normal_Abluminal_*` and `Diseased_Abluminal_*` reactions. These repeat some
  of the same rate terms (for example a second internalization of VEGF165:R1)
  and also carry the abluminal receptor insertion. Removing the duplicates moves
  normal-tissue VEGF165a from 4.59 to 3.16 pM, away from Table 1 (4.591 pM).
  This shows the authors' simulation included them, so they are kept.
* **Quirks of the export are kept as they are.** VEGF121:VEGFR2 in PAD calf is
  formed as `dis_V121_R2` but internalized from a separate, never-formed
  species `dis_R2_V121`. An orphan `dis_R1_N2` (always zero) feeds
  `dis_V121_R1_N2`. Both are inert or near-inert, and both are translated
  faithfully.
* **Excluded parts of the export.** The export also contains an unpublished
  anti-VEGF165b antibody arm: 34 reactions, its drug and complex species, and
  bevacizumab-derived parameters that the paper neither prints nor uses. With no
  dosing those species stay at zero. The arm is left out of the packaged model.
  Also left out are the output rule `hVEGF_free_dis_ug_per_ml`, whose fixed
  scale factor is not a valid conversion to ug/mL, and the 22 export species
  that no reaction touches.
* **Time unit.** The export works in seconds. The packaged model works in hours:
  every mass balance is multiplied by 3600, and rate constants keep their
  per-second values.
* **Blood-compartment and PAD-calf VEGF165b / VEGF121 levels** sit 9-26% below
  Table 1 and Figure 3 (see the Table 1 section). They were not tuned.
* **Mouse model not included.** The paper also simulates a mouse hindlimb
  ischemia version (Figure 6). It is built by swapping in mouse geometric
  parameters for all three compartments. Table 2 prints only the mouse calf
  geometry; the normal-tissue and blood geometry come from Finley 2013 (Front
  Oncol 3:196) and Yen 2011 (PLoS One 6:e27514), and no mouse model export is
  supplied. Only the human model is packaged here.
